title: Three Springs and One Short Gate
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）　|　核心词汇：grandparent　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 grandparent 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the child ① thanked a grandparent that no cousin in the lane would have described, and he said the thanking was the whole of the spring. The ② grandparent, meaning the elder itself and not the photograph, ran three springs and stayed undescribed in the book; a grandparent, he said, is the only thing in a lane that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ grandparent in that lane had the same short gate beside them, and the ④ grandparent at the far house, meaning the one they kept for the children to visit and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A grandparent, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the child said the describing is the part that fills three springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the grandparent was the whole of the matter, meaning the care and not the elder. The ⑥ grandparent, meaning the care and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; grandparent, he said, is either something you thank or the only word that means both an elder and a care. He said the care is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ grandparent had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short gate. The ⑧ grandparent of the whole thing, the child wrote in November, was one lane and three springs of describing; grandparent, he said, is either the one at the far house or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ grandparent I remember is the one described in the letter, which closed in 1971 and is still described as the quietest in the lane. A ⑩ grandparent, my mother said in 1973, is the only one that improves by being described; every grandparent, he said, is a care that has agreed to look like an elder. He said the care was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 祖父母；外祖父母（指巷子里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 祖父母；外祖父母（指那位长辈本人，与照片相对）
C. 固定搭配：thank a grandparent 向一位祖辈道谢
D. n. 祖辈（指留给孩子们去探望的那一位）
E. n. 祖辈（抽象总称，指一条巷子的祖辈之事）
F. n. 祖辈（指信里写到、被记下的那一位）
G. n. 祖辈的照拂（指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 照拂（抽象总称，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: thanked a grandparent that no cousin in the lane would have described
The grandparent, meaning the elder itself and not the photograph
the grandparent at the far house
the grandparent was the whole of the matter
the grandparent had become a line in a letter
The grandparent of the whole thing
A grandparent, my mother said in 1973

answers.why: thank a grandparent 意为“向一位祖辈道谢”，1964 年那个孩子向巷子里没有一位表亲肯描述的一位祖辈道了谢。
grandparent 意为“祖父母、外祖父母”，指那位长辈本人而不是照片，他经过了三个春天而在簿子上没有被描述。
grandparent 意为“祖父母、外祖父母”，指巷子里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一道矮矮的门。
grandparent 意为“祖辈”，指最远那座房子里留给孩子们去探望的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
grandparent 意为“祖辈的照拂”，指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份照拂就是那件事的全部。
grandparent 意为“照拂”，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位祖辈，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
grandparent 意为“祖辈”，指信里写到、被记下的那一位，到 1969 年这一位成了信里的一行。
grandparent 意为“祖辈”，孩子十一月写道，整件事的祖辈之事是一条巷子和三个春天的描述。
grandparent 意为“祖辈”，我记得的是信里描述过的那一位，1971 年过世了，至今仍被说成巷子里最安静的一位。
grandparent 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，一位祖辈是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
